old: The conch, whose father is Ratnākara, the mine of jewels, whose sister is Lakṣmī, would go about begging; what is not given does not present itself.
new: The conch, whose father is Ratnākara, the mine of jewels, whose sister is Lakṣmī, would go about begging; what is given does not present itself.
why: reviewer (error): Double negation: the Sanskrit has one na (na dattam upatiṣṭhate). 'Not given' plus 'does not' needs a second negation (adattam) that is not printed. Literal reading: 'what is given does not present itself'. The sense of the line is uncertain.

old: Line c ends with a hyphen (sarvajanto-) and line d begins reko: the split is sarvajantoḥ + ekaḥ (visarga becomes r before the next line's vowel). The genitive sarvajantoḥ is taken with bandhurā ('charming to every creature'); the alternative is to join it with the next clause. vyāla can mean serpent or beast of prey. new: Line c ends with a hyphen (sarvajanto-) and line d begins reko: the split is sarvajantoḥ + ekaḥ (visarga becomes r before the next line's vowel). The genitive sarvajantoḥ is taken with bandhurā ('charming to every creature'); the alternative is to join it with the next clause. vyāla can mean serpent or beast of prey. Ketakī is kept as a name and addressed; not identified. The printed bandhurasi has short a; the split bandhurā + asi (f., agreeing with ketaki) would normally be written bandhurāsi. The word is read as bandhurā + asi on sense; the vowel length is left as printed and not corrected.
why: reviewer (minor): The printed token is bandhurasi with short -a-. The split bandhurā + asi would give bandhurāsi (cf. the six -āpi forms in lines a and b, all with long ā). The mismatch is not recorded. No variant is claimed; only the discrepancy is noted.
